title: SAY IT BACK — the LangX reel
logline: A white caret types 'Hello' and edits it through three languages, then turns 57° and becomes the knife that cuts the reel open. Sixteen scripts each move the way they are read. A living grid of greetings folds into a chat where Sofia asks a question and the learner hesitates, makes a mistake and is corrected in green. The corrected line becomes an Echo card that hops the review ladder to 365 days. One quiet line then rewrites Merhaba as مرحبا, and 'Thank you' rolls through the app's eight languages. At the end two rivers of hellos bend along that same 57° line into the two arcs of the LangX mark, trade places in one 540° turn and lock on the downbeat of bar 21. 88 beats at 120 BPM (44 s).
signatureMotif:
THE CUT, and its partner THE TURN.

THE CUT is the straight line the mark's flat ends are cut on.
- Screen angles, y down, clockwise:
  - direction 147°: d = (-0.83867, 0.54464); read left to right it RISES about 33°: dUp = (0.83867, -0.54464);
  - normal 57°: n = (0.54464, 0.83867), which is also the direction of the mark's hard shadow.
- Derived once from MARK and added to core.js as REEL.CUT = { deg: 147, dUp, n }. It passes through the mark's CANVAS CENTRE (512,512), not through either arc centre.
  - The two flat-end lines sit ±2.35 canvas units either side of it: 1.1 px at the lockup scale.
  - Anywhere on stage, the Cut is 'the line through point P at 147°'. When no mark is on screen, P = (960,540).
- Arc centres for a mark whose canvas centre is P, at canvas scale k and rotation θ:
  - black = P + k·R(θ)·(79, -48.5);
  - white = P + k·R(θ)·(-79, 48.5).
  - Interpolate between these exact centres; never recompute an angle.
- Where the Cut appears:
  1. b0–8: born when the caret rotates +57° (from 90° to 147°) and stretches into it.
  2. b8: the only standard SLICE, owned by S2.
  3. Parallel echoes of it:
     - S2's Hebrew mask edge;
     - S3's reel-stop wave front;
     - S5's staircase slope;
     - S6's hairline, which WRITES Merhaba left to right, then walks back and writes مرحبا right to left;
     - S7's theme-sweep edge.
  4. b65–66: S7's yellow tab bar rotates -33° and becomes it again.
  5. b68: SPLIT-OPEN. The ink ground parts along it to reveal yellow, and it stays behind as a #201900 hairline.
  6. b80: in the finale it proves to be the line the arcs are cut on. The hairline retracts into the seam at the lock.

THE TURN: two things trade places by rotating 180°, the way the white arc is the black arc turned 180° about the canvas centre. It appears:
- b11–12.5: 'a' and 'o' orbit to turn Hallo into Hola;
- b10: S2's reading-direction arrow flips for Hebrew;
- b13–14: the Hangul row turns 90° and becomes the Japanese column (a quarter Turn);
- b74–80: the finale's 540° exchange of the black and white halves;
- b80.5–82.5: the X of the wordmark lands by a half-turn.

Rules the motif carries:
(a) The complete mark appears exactly ONCE, at the lock (b80). Before that only the Cut and the Turn allude to it.
(b) After the lock the mark never moves again.
(c) Full yellow ground appears only from b68. Before that yellow is at most ONE object per frame: the S3 cursor cell, the S7 tab bar and line.
(d) The hard 57° shadow belongs to the mark alone: #e0ac08 on yellow, #deab06 on ink. No type or UI ever carries it.

Bookend: the caret. It opens the reel (frame 0 is 'Hello|'), returns in S4 as the learner's hesitating cursor, and blinks once after the tagline before the final still.

styleBible.motionPrinciples:
1. Every move has three parts:
- ANTICIPATION: a lift, crouch or counter-turn of 4-10%, over 1/8 to 1/4 beat, with 'lift'.
- A DECISIVE ARRIVAL: either an overshoot ('pop' or 'spring') or a dead stop ('cut' into the beat).
- FOLLOW-THROUGH: a squash released on 'spring', or a lean that settles.
Nothing floats. No idle sine drift. No staggered fade-ins. Opacity is not a transition: things enter through masks, scale, draw or cut. Opacity is used only for echo trails and two-copy colour crossings.

2. RHYTHM
- Every hard cut and every landing falls on a beat or a subdivision (8th = 0.5 beat, 16th = 0.25, 32nd = 0.125).
- Big hits fall on bar lines: b16, b44, b68, b80.
- The piece autoplays muted, so the picture must carry the beat on its own.
- There is one 8th of total silence before each drop and before the lock: b15.75, b31.75, b67.75, b79.75.

3. STILLNESS IS A BEAT
- An outgoing frame that a slice or split-open replicates holds perfectly still for at least 0.5 beat.
- There is exactly one breath (S6, 4 s).
- The end card is still for the last 4 beats.

4. DETERMINISM
- Every visual is a pure function of the playhead.
- Randomness: ctx.rng(seed) with seed = 1000·sceneNumber + purpose index.
- Springs, hops, shakes and envelopes are closed-form:
  - hop: y = y0 + (y1-y0)·u - h·4u(1-u);
  - shake: A·e^(-t/τ)·sin(2πft);
  - kick envelope: e^(-6φ), where φ is the beat phase from ABSOLUTE time.
- Never accumulate per frame.
- No tl.call does visual work, and no CSS animations or transitions.
- Canvas draws read only the t they are given.
- A scene's timeline never runs past its slot, and scenes never overlap.

5. SPEED CAPS WITHOUT BLUR
- The mark and hero type (80 px or larger) turn at no more than about 300°/s.
- Anything the eye tracks moves at no more than about 4000 px/s.
- Exceptions:
  - exits leaving the frame;
  - the first 3 frames of a pull-back reveal;
  - the last 1/2 beat of a rotation that accelerates into a hard cut, which carries echo trails.
- Replacements for blur:
  - SPEED-STRETCH: scale along the motion by up to 1.2 at peak velocity.
  - ECHO TRAILS, only where a scene names them: 3 hard-edged ghost copies of the same element rendered at t-1/30, t-2/30 and t-3/30 s, at 30%, 15% and 6% opacity. Each ghost is the same closed-form state evaluated at the earlier time, so it seeks correctly.

6. SCRIPTS
- Split only Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, kana, Han and whole Hangul syllables.
- Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari and Thai move as whole words, behind masks.
- RTL words are revealed and travel right to left.

7. CRAFT
- Author text at its largest on-screen size and scale it down.
- Measure only after REEL.boot's font promise resolves.
- Dense fields (S3 grid, S8 rails) are Canvas2D or single SVG paths, never hundreds of transformed DOM nodes.
- Render the MP4 at 60 fps.
- With prefers-reduced-motion the page opens on the final lockup frame (b88).

eases.name: snap
eases.use: Decisive arrivals with no overshoot: masked rises, reveals, the camera landing, the bubble and card morphs, the hairline draw-in, the shadow snap at the lock. 0.2-0.45 s.

eases.name: pop
eases.use: Arrivals with about 10% overshoot: glyph pops, bubble pops, reel stops, odometer digit locks, dots, speaker glyph. Up to 0.25 s.

eases.name: whip
eases.use: Heavy-in, heavy-out travel: push-ins, card flights, the world-to-card contraction, conveyor slides, the tab bar becoming the Cut. Use it at least 0.5 s for large distances to respect the speed cap.

eases.name: cut
eases.use: Accelerating INTO a beat or off the frame: exits, the slice halves parting, collapses, the green strike landing on the beat, stamps (a dead stop, no overshoot), anything whose end is the hit.

eases.name: glide
eases.use: Controlled rotation and slow travel: every Turn (letter orbits, the 540° finale spin), the S6 hairline walks, the staircase draw, the finale camera. It is never used for idle drift.

eases.name: spring
eases.use: Closed-form damped spring with about 22% overshoot, then -6% and +2%, then settled. Used for landing squash releases, baseline dips, sags, the accent bounce and the 'tengo' hop. 0.25-0.5 s.

eases.name: lift
eases.use: Anticipations and the up-half of hops: lifts, crouches, counter-turns, wind-ups, squashes before a release. 1/8 to 1/4 beat.

styleBible.colorRules:
PALETTE: REEL.C tokens only. Do not invent shades.
- Grounds: deep #121318, ink #17191c, night #1c1f24, white #ffffff, fill #f4f5f7, green tint #e2f6ee, yellow #ffc409 (full ground ONLY in S8, from b68).
- Text: #17191c on light, #ffffff on dark, #201900 on yellow.
- Muted: #62676d on light, #9aa1a7 on dark.
- Hairlines and guides: #e8eaec on white, #2c3036 on dark.

THE MARK
- Arcs are always #000000 and #ffffff.
- It sits only on yellow (shadow #e0ac08) or ink (shadow #deab06).
- Shadow: 20 canvas units along 57° = (10.893, 16.773) canvas units, built by ctx.mark(). Its shadows group stays unrotated, so the shadow is always in screen space.
- To turn an arc, tween [arc, arcShadow] together with svgOrigin on the arc's centre. Never rotate g while the shadows are visible.
- No hard shadow on type, bubbles or cards, ever.

PRODUCT UI COLOURS
- Own bubble #e9f0fe; partner bubble #f4f5f7; bubble text #17191c.
- Corrections always #009f70, highlight #e2f6ee.
- Blue #3b6cf6 only for read aloud: speaker glyph, playhead, played bars.
- Streak orange and pro purple are not used.

YELLOW
- Before b68, at most ONE yellow object per frame: the S3 cursor cell, the S7 tab bar, the S7 Cut line.
- The film's first yellow ground is the split-open at b68.

PHOTOSENSITIVITY
- At most one full-frame ground or luminance change per beat, and never 3 in any 1 s window.
- Scheduled ground changes: b8, b10, b12, b14, b16 (grid), b32, b34-34.75 (green bloom), b36-37 (card contraction), b48-48.75 (white bloom), b56, b60.5, b62.5, b68.
- Fast montages change content, never the ground.
- Check the MP4 with a PEAT/Harding-style tool.

No gradients, glows, blur, neon, glass or CSS filters.

styleBible.transitionGrammar:
The runtime, core.js:
- A scene is visible only inside [start, start+dur).
- Later scenes paint over earlier ones on an opaque ground.
- Scenes never overlap.
- Every boundary is therefore OWNED BY THE INCOMING SCENE and is one of five types, each used deliberately:

1. HARD CUT ON THE BEAT WITH A MATCH
- b16 → no; that one is an identical frame (type 2).
- b32: colour-inverted, size-matched cut on 'estoy'.
- b56: hard contrast cut out of the breath into the manifesto slam.
- The incoming scene's frame 0 is specified to the pixel.

2. IDENTICAL-FRAME HANDOFF
The incoming scene's first frame is pixel-identical to the outgoing's last:
- b16: S3 pulls back from S2's frame, which becomes one grid cell;
- b24: S4 continues S3's bubble;
- b48: S6 starts on S5's dot.

3. SLICE (used exactly once, b8)
The incoming scene draws a REPLICA of the outgoing still frame as two clip-path halves on each side of the Cut through (960,540), over its own composed world. Relative to the incoming scene's beat 0:
- 0.0 to 2 frames: the replica's line flashes from 3 to 12 px and back;
- 0.0-0.125: the halves slip 24 px along ±dUp (upper-left half +dUp, lower-right half -dUp), 'snap';
- 0.125-0.75: the halves part 1200 px along ∓n (upper-left along -n, lower-right along +n), 'cut'.

4. SPLIT-OPEN (used exactly once, b68)
- The incoming scene draws the outgoing ink ground as two half-plane plates meeting on the Cut.
- The Cut line flashes to 12 px for 2 frames.
- The plates part: upper-left by (-343.3, -969.4), lower-right by (+343.3, +969.4), 'snap', 0.75 beat.
- The line stays behind in the world.

5. BLOOM FROM THE POINT OF EXCHANGE
A disc grows out of the exact point where something was exchanged or corrected, and the new ground arrives inside it:
- b34: green tint out of the correction;
- b48: white out of the ember.
- Any object crossing a bloom edge exists as two copies with complementary clips, so its colour flips exactly at the edge.
- Call ctx.ground(newColour) on the frame the disc covers the stage.

Inside scenes, the same vocabulary applies:
- carried-element morphs: cell → bubble, card → dot, tab bar → Cut;
- match cuts on shape: horizontal Hangul → vertical kana.

No more than one slice and one split-open in the film. Never two identical transitions back to back.

Verify every boundary with snap.mjs --boundaries.

scenes.title: Caret — the cursor edits, then becomes the knife
scenes.synopsis:
Frame 0 is the thumbnail: 'Hello|' in white on deep ink.

The caret waits, steps back like an arrow key, and turns Hello into Hallo by swapping one letter. Then 'a' and 'o' orbit each other to make Hola (the Turn in two letters), while the dropped 'l' dents a spring-loaded baseline. The H is flicked away and an accent falls onto the 'a': Olá.

The caret then rotates 57° and stretches into the infinite Cut line lying across the word. The first product idea (one greeting, many languages, exchanged) lands inside 3 seconds.
scenes.shotList:
All beats are relative to the scene start (b0). Ground #121318.

SETUP (frame 0, the thumbnail)
- WORD: 'Hello', Nunito 800, 300 px, tracking -0.02em, #ffffff. Each letter is its own span (SplitText chars), horizontally centred on x=960 by measured advance, baseline y=646.
- CARET: #ffffff rect 12×190, left edge 16 px after the word's right ink edge, spanning y 445-635.
- ANNOTATION: 'EN · LATIN' plus an SVG → arrow, Nunito 800 24 px, tracking 0.12em, #9aa1a7, left x=120, baseline 134.
- Nothing moves on frame 0.

TIMELINE
- 0.0-2.0 COUNT-IN: the caret blinks with hard steps via tl.set: on 0-0.5, off 0.5-1.0, on 1.0-1.5, off 1.5-2.0. The word is dead still.
- 2.0 / 2.25 / 2.5 ARROW KEYS: the caret is on and jumps (tl.set, no tween) one character left on each 16th: to l|o, then l|l, then e|l, measured from the glyph boxes.
- 3.0-3.5 BASELINE GUIDE: a 1 px #2c3036 line at y=646 draws in from the left, x 120 → 1800 (DrawSVG, 'snap').
- 3.0 HELLO→HALLO:
  - 'e' drops down out of its own glyph-box mask (yPercent 0→110, 'cut', 0.12 s).
  - 'a' drops in from above (yPercent -110→0, 'pop', 0.2 s).
  - Letters to its right shift by the measured width difference ('snap', 0.2 s).
  - The caret jumps to a|l.
  - The annotation rolls EN→DE.
- 3.5: the caret goes off and stays hidden.
- 3.75-4.0 ANTICIPATION: 'a' (index 1) and 'o' (index 4) lift 10 px ('lift').
- 4.0-5.0 THE TURN IN MINIATURE:
  - 'a' and 'o' orbit 180° clockwise about their shared midpoint, 'a' over the top and 'o' under the baseline. Positions only; the glyphs stay upright. 'glide', 0.5 s, peak under 2600 px/s.
  - Each lands with a 4 px vertical settle ('spring', 0.2 s).
- 4.25 THE DROP: the second 'l' (index 3) falls through the baseline: y +700, rotation 18°, 'cut', 0.35 s.
  - Where it crosses, the baseline guide dips 16 px at that x and springs back ('spring', 0.4 s, a closed-form bump confined to ±120 px around the fall point).
- 4.5-5.0: the remaining four glyphs close up and re-centre to form 'Hola', centred on 960 ('snap'). They lock on 5.0. The annotation rolls DE→ES.
- 5.5-6.5 HOLA→OLÁ:
  - 5.5: 'H' leans +6° about its baseline ('lift', 0.06 s).
  - 5.625: 'H' is flicked off to the left: x -700, rotation -40°, 'cut', 0.2 s. As an exit it may exceed the speed cap; it gets speed-stretch scaleX 1.2.
  - 5.75: 'o' rolls to 'O' inside its glyph mask ('pop', 0.12 s). 'O', 'l' and 'a' close up and re-centre on 960 ('snap', lands 6.25).
  - 5.9: a detached acute accent falls from y -200. It is a clipped copy of the 'á' glyph showing only what is above the x-height line minus 4 px, 1.3× size, #ffffff.
  - The accent lands on the 'a' at 6.25 and bounces twice: 18 px, then 6 px, landing 6.375 and 6.5 (closed-form hop, then 'spring').
  - On 6.5 the plain 'a' plus the accent are swapped for the real 'á' glyph (pixel-identical).
  - The annotation rolls ES→PT.
- 6.5-6.75: the baseline guide retracts to the right ('cut').
- 6.75: the caret reappears (tl.set) 16 px after 'Olá'.
- 6.75-6.875: the caret counter-turns -6° about its centre ('lift').
- 6.875-7.5 THE CARET BECOMES THE CUT, all 'snap':
  - it rotates to +57° (its long axis goes from 90° to 147°);
  - its length grows 190 → 2600 px;
  - its thickness thins 12 → 3 px;
  - its centre travels to (960,540).
  - It now lies exactly on REEL.CUT through (960,540), rising 33° to the right across 'Olá'.
- 7.5-8.0: everything holds perfectly still. This is the frame S2 replicates.

scenes.title: Relay — every script moves the way it is read
scenes.synopsis:
The caret's Cut slices Olá in half. Through the gap, seven scripts relay the greeting, each entering the way it is read:
- Cyrillic rises left to right.
- Greek inhales into place.
- Hebrew is revealed right to left, and the arrow turns.
- Devanagari hangs from its headline bar.
- Korean syllables stamp in.
- The Hangul row turns 90° and cuts on the beat into the vertical Japanese column.
- 你好 slams down with a camera shake.
The ground changes only on even beats.

A typographic chat, not a phone mockup. Sofia's 'Hola' grows into '¡Hola! ¿Tienes hambre?'.

The learner's own blue-tint bubble opens with the caret from the cold open. 'Sí,' comes out quickly; then the caret blinks twice and the beat drops out, a hesitation acted purely in timing. Then 'estoy hambre.' is rushed out and sent.

scenes.title: Green pen — the corrected line climbs the ladder
scenes.synopsis:
A colour-inverted, size-matched hard cut strands the mistake, white on ink, in silence. A hand-drawn green line strikes it exactly on the beat. The struck word steps back and 'tengo' rises in green, and the world blooms green from the point of correction.

The sentence reassembles as 'Sí, tengo hambre.', and the green world contracts into a white Echo card on the night ground. The card reads itself aloud: its letters turn into waveform bars that pulse with the kick, with the corrected word still green inside the sound.

Then the card shrinks and hops up the review ladder: '10 minutes', '1 day', three quick hops across the '…', and one big leap onto '365 days' as the odometer locks on the downbeat. Finally the card condenses into a single white ember.

scenes.title: The Eight — manifesto, and thank you in every interface language
scenes.synopsis:
A hard contrast cut out of the breath. Three lines slam onto ink, one per beat: 'No ads.', 'Real people.', 'Open source.'. Their full stops fall off and bounce away.

Then 'Thank you' flips through the app's eight interface languages on every 8th. Each word is wiped in its own reading direction, and a yellow tab bar caterpillars under the language codes. Mid-roll, a diagonal edge at the Cut angle sweeps the frame to light theme, and two beats later back to dark, without the roll missing a step.

Finally the yellow tab bar turns -33° and stretches into the Cut line itself.

scenes.title: Exchange — the hellos bend into the mark
scenes.synopsis:
DROP 2. The ink ground splits open along the Cut and reveals the film's first yellow. The line stays behind as a hairline.

Two rivers of hellos, black Latin and white non-Latin scripts, stream in opposite directions on rails parallel to it. The rails bend at constant length into two arc bands. Then the pair makes one 540° turn while the camera pulls back into the lockup position, and the bands are inked into the solid black and white arcs.

On the downbeat of bar 21 they lock: the hard shadow snaps out and the hairline retracts into the seam. It was the line the mark is cut on all along.

The wordmark rises with a half-turning X, the tagline follows, the caret blinks once, and the frame holds still.

MARK GEOMETRY
- A 'turn group' (SVG) uses transform translate(P) rotate(ρ) scale(S) translate(-512,-512), in the mark's 1024 canvas units.
- P starts at (960,540), ρ at 180 (swapped), S at 1.4.
- It has NO shadows.

0.0 SPLIT-OPEN (the only one):
- S8 draws, on top, two #121318 half-plane plates meeting on the Cut through (960,540), with the 4 px #ffc409 line on the seam: pixel-identical to S7.
- Frames 0-1: the yellow line is 12 px, then it is removed.
- 0.0-0.75: the upper-left plate moves by (-343.3,-969.4) and the lower-right by (+343.3,+969.4) ('snap').
- Beneath, S8's world: ground #ffc409, the rails mid-stream, and a 1.5 px #201900 HAIRLINE on the Cut through P, 2600 px long.

0.0-4.0 RAILS (inside the turn group, canvas units; each rail is 607.6 units = π·193.4 long):
- BLACK rail: text 'Hello · Merhaba · Hola · Hallo · Bonjour · Привет · Olá · Ciao · ' repeated, Nunito 900, #000000.
  - Midpoint (485.7,301.3) canvas = the black arc's centreline at 237°.
  - On stage at ρ=180 that is the lower-right rail, midpoint (996.8,835).
- WHITE rail: text 'こんにちは · 안녕하세요 · 你好 · नमस्ते · สวัสดี · שלום · مرحبا · Γειά σου · ' repeated, Noto 800 families, #ffffff.
  - Midpoint (538.3,722.7) canvas; on stage the upper-left rail, midpoint (923.1,245).
  - Each RTL word is isolated in its own tspan (direction rtl, unicode-bidi isolate).
- Both rails are tangent to their arc's centreline at the midpoint, so they are parallel to the Cut.
- Text is 67 canvas units (94 px on stage), vertically centred on the path via dominant-baseline, and reads up-right on stage.
- No shadows on the rails.
- STREAM: the textPath startOffset runs linearly ('none'), 200 units per beat, black rail up-right and white rail down-left, with seeded starting offsets.
- Each beat 0,1,2,3 adds a +43-unit surge ('snap', 0.25 beat).
- The hairline pulses 1.5→4→1.5 px on each beat ('snap' up, 'cut' down within 0.25 beat).
- The rails' ends are hard cuts: text simply appears and disappears there.

4.0-6.0 THE BEND (constant length, 'glide'):
- Curvature κ goes 0 → 1/193.4.
- Each rail is recomputed every frame as an arc of fixed length 607.6 through its midpoint, bending toward its own arc centre. Use a straight line while |κ| < 1e-4.
- At 6.0 the rails ARE the arc centrelines: black = arcStroke(591,463.5,193.4,147,327), white = arcStroke(433,560.5,193.4,327,507). The text keeps streaming along them.

6.0-12.0 THE TURN:
- 6.0-6.25: wind-up, ρ 180→174 ('lift').
- 6.25-12.0: ρ 174→720 ('glide', 2.875 s; peak about 298°/s; one direction; decelerates once; dead stop on 12.0).
- 6.0-12.0 camera, both 'glide': P travels (960,540)→(401.3,493.8), and S goes 1.4→0.46875. The hairline is always drawn through the current P at 147°.
- INK-IN:
  - 7.0-8.5: a #000000 stroke, width 83.8, butt caps, along the black centreline (DrawSVG 0→100%, 'whip');
  - 7.5-9.0: the same in #ffffff for the white arc.
  - Letters are covered as the stroke passes. At 9.0 the rails are hidden.
- ECHO TRAILS on the two solid strokes only, 9.0-11.0.

12.0 LOCK (b80, bar 21 downbeat):
- On this frame the turn group is replaced by ctx.mark(layer, {x:401.3, y:493.8, size:480, shade:'#e0ac08'}). At ρ=720 its geometry is identical to the group's.
- Its shadows group translate starts at (0,0) and snaps to (10.893,16.773) canvas units (5.1, 7.9 px) ('snap', 0.25 s).
- The hairline retracts both ends into P (401.3,493.8), where it passes through the seam between the flat ends (DrawSVG, 'cut', 0.25 s).
- From here the mark never moves.

12.5-14.5 WORDMARK:
- The outlined letters from lockup-horizontal.svg sit in a group with transform translate(161.3,253.8) scale(0.46875), fill #17191c.
- Each letter rises 60 px through a clip whose edge is parallel to the Cut, so it reveals corner-first ('snap', 0.4 s): L at 12.5, a at 12.75, n at 13.0, g at 13.25.
- X: it rotates in-plane 180°→0 about its centre, (1556.1,472.2) on stage, over 12.5-14.5 ('glide', peak about 283°/s). It rises through its clip over 13.5-14.5. It lands on 14.5, completing the final half-turn.

14.5-15.5 TAGLINE: 'The friendly way to practise a language with real people', Nunito 700 40 px, #201900, centred on x=960, baseline 740. Its words rise from a line mask ('snap', 1/32 stagger).

15.5-16.0: a #201900 caret, 4×44 px, 8 px after 'people', covering the tagline's cap height, is ON (tl.set on 15.5, off on 16.0). The bookend.

16.0-20.0: nothing moves. The b88 frame is the resting frame and the poster.
